thread:
rachel-sales: ACME POC reporting 401s after switching to what they believe is an org key. They include X-Redwood-Org and X-Redwood-Project. Without headers the same secret sometimes works. Can we triage?

matt-eng: Paste the sanitized curl + last 8 of key id please.

rachel-sales: Heres the curl they used:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx-9a7b6c2d\" \
  -H \"X-Redwood-Org: acme-corp\" \
  -H \"X-Redwood-Project: demo-app\" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hey"}'
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 401 {"error":{"code":"invalid_key","message":"key not valid for requested org"}}

anya-platform: Last 8 `9a7b6c2d` shows a service-account-style key created in the ACME personal workspace with binding to project `demo`. Our lookup says its not an org-scoped key.

lucas-se: Two likely causes: 1) key is user- or project-scoped and header org slug doesn't match, or 2) key secret rotated but the app still uses cached old secret. They said it \"sometimes\" works which hints at a rolling deployment with mixed secrets.

rachel-sales: They mentioned they deployed a new podset with the rotated secret last night and then rolled back. Could that cause intermittent 401s?

matt-eng: Yes. If some pods have old personal key and others have new org key, behavior will differ depending on whether the request includes X-Redwood-Org. Also note header casing: some proxies lowercase headers and our authproxy expects exact header names; but we canonicalize so unlikely. More common: duplicate headers from a load balancer inject different project vals.

ci-bot: deploy rollout acme-demo v2.3 -> 8/12 pods ready, 4 still on previous revision

anya-platform: That CI note explains intermittent. Action plan: a) confirm which pods have which envvar value, b) create an ephemeral org-scoped key for them to validate a clean run, c) recommend secret rollout strategy (atomic or blue/green).

lucas-se: Also check key scopes. If they created an org key but accidentally checked \"generate only\" then calls to /v1/embeddings will return 403 insufficient_scope, which can confuse troubleshooting. Ask if they are calling multiple endpoints.

rachel-sales: They are calling both generate and embeddings, yes.

matt-eng: Quick tests for them to run (sanitized):
```
# test generate
curl -s -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-org-TEST123\" \
  -H \"X-Redwood-Org: acme-corp\" \
  -d '{"prompt":"ping"}'
# test embeddings
curl -s -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-org-TEST123\" \
  -H \"X-Redwood-Org: acme-corp\" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1","input":"foo"}'
```
If generate 200 but embeddings 403 then scope is the culprit. If both 401 when org header present then binding mismatch.

anya-platform: I created a short-lived org-scoped key sk-org-ephemeral-7c41 (expires in 24h) and validated both endpoints. Sending it over our secure channel for their screen-share.

ci-bot: secret created sk-org-ephemeral-7c41 -> expires 24h

matt-eng: Also a note about service accounts and KMS: if they use KMS to decrypt the secret at startup and older pods still have the old decrypted value, you can see mixed behavior. Recommend checking /var/run/secrets or env via kubectl describe pod to confirm.

lucas-se: FYI: project vs org binding rules: org keys require X-Redwood-Org to match the org slug exactly; project-scoped keys require X-Redwood-Project to match the project slug. If both headers are present we validate both. Mismatches yield 403 project_mismatch or 401 invalid_key depending on binding.

rachel-sales: They asked whether we can programmatically patch a key to add scopes instead of creating new one.

anya-platform: We currently do not allow mutating scopes on an existing secret via the Console UI for audit reasons. Use key rotation: create new key with desired scopes and then revoke the old one after validation. We can add that to the one-pager.

matt-eng: Quick troubleshooting checklist I'll add to the support call script: 1) verify key id suffix and binding in our system, 2) confirm pod images/envs reflect new secret (no old pods), 3) run the two curl tests above, 4) if intermittent, drain and restart pods to ensure atomic rollout, 5) create ephemeral org key for validation, 6) if still failing attach the authproxy logs (we need request-id).

lucas-se: To collect logs ask them to include X-Request-ID/Unguessable correlation id and set DEBUG_AUTH=true in a dev pod so we can see key lookup path. We log key binding and scope checks (we'll redact secrets).

rachel-sales: Great. Screen share scheduled in 45m. Can someone from platform join to walk the k8s secret roll?

anya-platform: I'll join. I'll also draft the one-pager with best practices: prefer org keys for POCs, scope minimally but not overly restrict during dev, store secrets server-side (k8s/Vault), use atomic secret rollouts, rotate via CI pipeline, revoke old keys after validation, monitor Console for token usage and 429s.

ci-bot: ticket POC-9988 created, priority P2

rachel-sales: Post-call update: we found mixed pods running the old secret. We drained and restarted the cluster, validated using the ephemeral org key, then created a permanent org key in their Console and rolled it out atomically. Both /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings return 200. Customer also asked for a short invoice estimate for burst Dedicated capacity; looping sales-ops. Closing this thread unless more issues crop up.
